summary.text: Abbas Alawieh is the Democratic candidate for Michigan State Senate District 2 in the November 3, 2026 general election, after winning the August 4 Democratic primary over Erin Byrnes.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a former congressional chief of staff and said his central policy priority is "Working Families First."

paragraphs.text: Alawieh earned a high school diploma from Fordson High School, a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor in 2014, and a graduate degree from the University of Michigan School of Public Health in 2017.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he served as chief of staff to U.S. Rep. Cori Bush (D-MO) and as a senior legislative staffer to U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI) and Andy Levin (D-MI).
He also said he was a Democratic National Convention delegate in 2024 after leading the Uncommitted movement.
Alawieh said he moved back to Michigan to care for his mother after her cancer diagnosis and that he lives in Dearborn with his wife, Amanda.
Alawieh won the Democratic primary with 58.9% of the vote (23,722 votes) to Byrnes's 41.1% (16,567 votes).

In his survey responses, Alawieh listed lowering health care costs and Medicare for All, universal childcare and pre-K, investment in roads and mass public transportation, and expanded affordable housing among the areas he wants to work on.
